text:
anya: Ran a KV-only quantization sweep on model 'open-13b-v1' this morning. FP8 and INT8 applied only to KV cache (values only), model weights left in FP16. Sharing quick numbers and a couple of config snippets.
matt: Nice. What's the test rig and workload?
sophie: Also, cold vs warm cache? those usually diverge a lot.
anya: Test rig: 1xA100-40GB, inference threads=8, dynamic batching off. Workload: streaming chat traces, avg seq_len=512, prompt tokens=64, gen=448. Warm = after 1 full conversation, cold = first request after model load.
anya: FP8-KV: memory for KV dropped ~46% (compared to FP16-KV). INT8-KV: ~65% drop.
anya: Latency summary (median / p95, single-request streaming):
- FP16-KV baseline: 45ms / 220ms
- FP8-KV: 48ms / 280ms
- INT8-KV: 55ms / 340ms
matt: So FP8 adds small median overhead but p95 jumps — is that dequantization on hot path causing spikes?
sophie: Looks like dequantize per attention block is the culprit; when KV is warm the median is fine, but cold (first few tokens) we pay more as we materialize caches.
anya: Correct. Warm median for FP8 is ~46ms, warm p95 ~210ms (so p95 gap mostly cold). INT8 has a larger overhead due to more complex scaling logic in our current kernel.
ruth: Any quality regressions? ran our 500-example eval set?
anya: Ran eval A/B (unquantized vs FP8-KV vs INT8-KV) on 500 instruction-following prompts. BLEU-ish task-wise deltas: FP8 avg metric delta ~-0.2%, INT8 ~-0.9%. Most regressions concentrated on long-context retrieval prompts where KV precision matters.
anya: For safety thresholds: FP8 passes our 0.5% regression gate, INT8 fails on that gate but passes a 1.0% lenient gate.
matt: Configs? quick example of how I ran it:
```
./run_infer --model open-13b-v1 --kv-quant=fp8 --kv-quant-granularity=per_head --sequence_len=512 --streaming=true
```
For INT8 change --kv-quant=int8 and add --kv-dequant-blend=0.2 (we used 0.2 to soften cold hits).
sophie: Did you test per-tensor vs per-head? per-head usually preserves quality but costs a touch more memory.
anya: Yep: per-tensor FP8 reduces memory a bit more (~3%) but FP8-per-head keeps metric delta to -0.15% vs -0.2% for per-tensor. Tradeoff seems worthwhile.
ruth: For deployment guidance: Hosted API should default to FP16-KV for latency-sensitive tiers, offer FP8-KV as opt-in (better mem, small p95 risk). For Dedicated we can expose INT8-KV behind a config flag for customers that want max density but must accept ~1% risk.
matt: Also add automatic fallback: if p95 > X or error rate rises, runtime toggles KV back to FP16 for that model instance.
anya: Agreed. I'll open a draft PR that adds:
- perf docs with median/p95 numbers for cold/warm
- runtime flag knobs (--kv-quant, --kv-dequant-blend, --kv-quant-granularity)
- an automated health-check that flips to FP16 when latency/regressions exceed thresholds
deploy-bot: Deployment check created: #3421 (kv-quant-sweep docs) - reviewer: @sophie.
anya: Next steps: run longer sweep across seq_len 128/512/1024, load=concurrent 1/4/8, and add the 2k prompt eval set Ruth proposed. Will report back mid-day tomorrow. :eyes:
